title: Split the DuplicateBodySampleId validation code for duplicates vs out-of-order ids
description:
Source: docs/tasks/tickets/CC-078-split-duplicate-body-sample-id-code.md
Source key: CC-078
Source status: Backlog
Source priority: P3

## Summary

`ValidationCode.DuplicateBodySampleId` is emitted for two distinct problems:
an actually duplicated sample id and an out-of-order (non-monotonic) id list.
Both are reported with the same code, which blurs the diagnostic meaning.

## Scope

- Either split into two codes (e.g. `DuplicateBodySampleId` and
  `OutOfOrderBodySampleId`) or document why one code intentionally covers both.
- Keep the validator report-only: no repair, no silent rewrite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Duplicate and out-of-order cases produce distinguishable diagnostics.
- Existing serialized definitions and tests remain valid.
- No behavior change beyond the diagnostic code.

## Validation

- Validator PlayMode tests assert the distinct codes for each case.

## Findings

Raised as finding 2.3 in the 2026-08-24 audit addendum. Low urgency; the current
single code still flags the invalid DNA, it just does not say which problem it is.

## Blockers

None.

## Next Step

Add the second code and adjust the emitting check plus tests.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Round 3 (final) implementation complete. Design decision: SPLIT. Added ValidationCode.OutOfOrderBodySampleId directly after DuplicateBodySampleId. Adjusted the emitting check in DefinitionValidator.ValidateBody so the two checks are if/else-if: a reused sample Id (HashSet Add fails) -> DuplicateBodySampleId; a unique-but-non-monotonic Id (<= previous sample) -> OutOfOrderBodySampleId. Report-only: no repair, no rewrite, no schema/serialization/generation change. This keeps the two problems distinguishable and mutually exclusive for typical cases (a genuine duplicate [1,2,1] reports only Duplicate; a unique scramble [1,3,2] reports only OutOfOrder). Tests: strengthened Validate_DetectsDuplicateBodySampleIds (asserts Duplicate present AND OutOfOrder absent) and rewrote the old Validate_DetectsNonIncreasingBodySampleIds (which had actually constructed a duplicate [1,1]) into Validate_DetectsOutOfOrderBodySampleIds (unique evenly-spaced [1,3,2], asserts OutOfOrder present AND Duplicate absent).

Focused PlayMode discriminating tests: 2/2 passed (Validate_DetectsDuplicateBodySampleIds, Validate_DetectsOutOfOrderBodySampleIds). Full Runtime PlayMode suite: 526/526 passed. EditMode suite (ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor): 131/131 passed. dotnet builds (--no-restore, all exit 0): ProceduralCreature.Runtime, ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime, ProceduralCreature.Editor. git diff --check: clean (exit 0). Not committed/pushed (orchestrator owns commit); nothing staged.
